about:
compose@3: cover poles with conditions. Each pole's sampled strong activations (events/sample.py) are matched against
the condition library (conds.py: domain gates, part of speech, morphology, grammatical roles, code syntax roles); a
hypothesis is selected only when it already covers at least half of the pole, so a hold is assignment-grade by
construction (the survey's 50% rule, docs/HARNESS.md).

  python -m bonsai_interp.compose.round3 protocol    # write the manifest; commit it ALONE
  python -m bonsai_interp.compose.round3 select      # CPU: hypotheses from the event sample (selection split)
  python -m bonsai_interp.compose.round3 build       # CPU: held-out 8 + 8 tests from the test split; commit the prereg ALONE
  python -m bonsai_interp.compose.round3 score       # GPU: grammar/run.py's scorer (quick-8+8@2, 3 preambles)
  python -m bonsai_interp.compose.round3 report      # CPU
  (--smoke DIR: no manifests, files in DIR, at most --max hypotheses; its pairs come from the selection split)

Hypotheses, per eligible pole not already assignment-grade, with >= SEL["min_events"] sampled strong activations in at
least SEL["min_windows"] windows:
  1. Condition c: its coverage (share of the pole's sampled activations where c holds) >= SEL["min_cov"] and its lift
     (coverage / c's base rate over the sampled windows) >= SEL["min_lift"]. The pole's c is the one with the highest
     precision among those: the share of c's positions in the sampled windows where the pole is strong (coverage x the
     pole's strong count / c's count). Coverage says c explains the pole; precision says c fires it, which a held-out
     8 + 8 needs (the selection-split pilot, 2026-10-27: below 0.1, 1 of 103 tests held; at 0.1 or more, 15 of 55).
  2. Tokens: T = the fewest of the pole's commonest tokens (where c holds) that cover SEL["token_share"] of those
     activations, at most SEL["max_tokens"]. When c and T together still cover >= SEL["min_cov"] of the pole, the
     hypothesis is the conjunction "a token of T where c holds" (kind conj), tested as the same token with c on against c
     off: it holds only if c matters beyond the token. Otherwise it is c alone (kind class), tested against tokens of the
     same corpus-frequency band where c fails, in the same domain, and in c's natural complement where its pass defines
     one (sweeplib@3/4/5's quiet side: present against past verbs, plain against superlative adjectives, the same word in
     another grammatical role, code tokens outside the code role).
  A conjunction also needs c to matter within T: the share of the pole's activations on T where c holds must be at least
  SEL["min_lift_in_tokens"] times the share of all of T's positions where c holds (otherwise it is the word pole again).
  A hypothesis needs precision >= SEL["min_precision"] (for a conjunction, over the positions where c holds on a token of
  T). Hypotheses are ranked by coverage x precision; the best SEL["cap"] are tested. Each test has a placebo (two snippets
  where c fails, same keys) read on the same pole.

events.doc:
A uniform sample of every pole's strong activations over the parsed and lexed windows (GPU, one pass, all 36 layers).

  python -m bonsai_interp.events.sample run [--limit W] [--out FILE]   # -> data/events/bonsai1.events.npz
  python -m bonsai_interp.events.sample stats                          # CPU: counts per layer

The windows are those the grammar pass parsed (12,000 English windows of the selection split, grammar/parse.py) and those
sweeplib@5 lexed (every code window of the selection split, codesyn/lex.py), so any condition defined on the parse or the lex
can be evaluated at every sampled activation. Activations are read at full window context (1,024 tokens) from position
RULE["min_pos"] on (window starts are an artifact, FINDINGS 2026-10-18).

A strong activation is >= RULE["strong"] (0.3) of the pole's corpus maximum (the scan's), in the pole's sign. Per pole the
pass keeps the K = 64 strong activations with the smallest hash of their (window, position): a bottom-k sample, uniform over
the pole's strong activations and shared between poles (two poles that fire at one position keep it or drop it together,
when both have enough). It also counts every pole's strong activations by domain. Weak poles (corpus max < 0.5) are skipped.

Per pole (layer, sign, neuron): ids (K) int32 = window * 1024 + position (-1 empty), vals (K) float16 = activation / pole max,
count (int64, all strong activations), count_dom (English, code).

condition_doc:
compose@4's condition library: compose@3's (conds.py, unchanged) plus text-format conditions and every condition shifted
to the previous token and the one before it. CPU only. The same interface as conds.py (names, at, population, _parse,
_lex, _english, _code), so compose@3's engine runs on it.

  fmt:line_start      the first token of a line            fmt:sent_start   the first word after . ! or ?
  fmt:digit           a token of digits                    fmt:after_digit  right after one
  fmt:capitalized     a capitalized word (Word)            fmt:allcaps      an all-capitals word (WORD)
  fmt:punct           a punctuation-only token             fmt:after_punct  right after one
  fmt:in_parens       inside ( ) or [ ] opened on the same line
  fmt:in_quote        inside a quotation opened on the same line (straight quotes by parity, curly quotes by pairs)
  fmt:url             in a URL (from http or www to the next whitespace)
  fmt:list_line       on a line that opens with -, *, • or a number      fmt:header_line  on a line that opens with #
  prev1:C, prev2:C    compose@3's condition C holds at the token 1 or 2 back (domain gates excluded)
Format conditions apply in both domains; a shifted condition applies in its own condition's domain.
read: last token, mean over the 3 PREAMBLES (grammar/run.py score, unchanged)
test_split: English windows parsed by the grammar pass (bonsai1.parse.test.npz) and code windows lexed by sweeplib@5 (bonsai1.lex.test.npz)
coverage: the selected hypothesis's share of the pole's sampled strong activations (selection split)
about4:
compose@4: compose@3's cover (round3.py, unchanged) with a wider condition library (conds2.py): text-format conditions
and every compose@3 condition shifted to the previous token and the one before it. The event sample is compose@3's
(pinned by hash), so no new GPU sampling pass is needed.

  python -m bonsai_interp.compose.round4 protocol | select | build | score | report   (same stages and flags as round3.py)

Two differences beyond the library:
  1. Poles compose@3 tested are left out, as well as every assignment-grade pole (which now includes compose@3's holds).
     A re-test could repeat compose@3's pairs exactly (an item set's seed is its key).
  2. The aim is the layers every round has found hardest (12-17): mid-layer poles whose strong activations spread over
     many read tokens and whose read-token conditions cover little (the 2026-10-27 diagnostic: at L14 and L16 only 7-14%
     of poles have a read-token condition covering half of them; shifted and format conditions roughly double that).
excluded: assignment-grade poles (atlas, after compose@3) and every pole compose@3 tested
